questions.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}-5{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{2}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{3}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
-3{x}_{2}^{2}\le 2{x}_{2}^{2},\,-5{x}_{3}^{2}\le 2{x}_{3}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}-5{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \le 2{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=2(1)=2.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\le 2.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no greater than $2.$ But before we conclude that $2$ is the maximum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=2.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}-5{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =2(1)^{2}-3(0)^{2}-5(0)^{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the maximum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $2.$

$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$

questions.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=-3{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}+5{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{1}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{3}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
-3{x}_{1}^{2}\ge -4{x}_{1}^{2},\,5{x}_{3}^{2}\ge -4{x}_{3}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =-3{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}+5{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge -4{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}-4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-4({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-4({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=-4(1)=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge -4.$   

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $-4.$ But before we conclude that $-4$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=-4.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =-3{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}+5{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-3(0)^{2}-4(1)^{2}+5(0)^{2} \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $-4.$

questions.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of the matrix $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 4 \\ 4 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -15 & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)(\lambda -5) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =-3,\,5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}=5.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-5{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =2(0)^{2}-5(0)^{2}+3(1)^{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| =1,$ the maximum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})$ is equal to $3.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Minimum Value Given a Canonical Form on the Unit Sphere
canonical_examples.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})=5x_1^2 - 4x_2^2 - 6x_3^2$ given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| =1.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that $x_1^2 \geq 0$ and $x_2^2 \geq 0.$ So, we have that

$$
5x_1^2 \geq -6x_1^2, \qquad -4x_2^2 \geq -6x_2^2.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}-6{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge -6{x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{2}^{2}-6{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-6({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $\| \mathbf{x} \| = 1$ is equivalent to $x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 =1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-6({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=-6(1)=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(\mathbf{x}) \geq -6.$

So, the value of $Q(\mathbf{x})$ can be no smaller than $-6.$ But before we conclude that $-6$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(\mathbf{x}) = -6.$

Notice that when ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070559/assets/d509eb79bc8d9a96b60922166e49d0225eac7a99d2614859c31af15199d4d47c.png) we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}-6{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =5(0)^{2}-4(0)^{2}-6(1)^{2} \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| =1,$ the minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})$ is equal to $-6.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Quadratic Form on the Unit Sphere
canonical_examples.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})=x_1^2-2x_2^2-2x_3^2+2x_2x_3$  given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| = 1.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\max \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{max}}
$$

- The minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\min \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{min}}
$$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070559/assets/d7716e2c2924212e880275dd674d4a951daf66ac41e5a888a57acb6be686118f.png)

Now, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of the matrix $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )(-2-\lambda )-1) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +3) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(\lambda +3)(\lambda +1) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =1,\,-1,\,-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\min \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = -3.
$$
